关键词: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
主要内容: On October 30, 2019, the Federal Reserve Board issued an Implementation Note outlining the decisions made to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC). The Board of Governors voted unanimously to lower the interest rate paid on required and excess reserve balances to 1.55 percent, effective October 31, 2019. The FOMC also directed the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account to maintain the federal funds rate within a target range of 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent. Additionally, the FOMC authorized the purchase of Treasury bills through the second quarter of next year and the conduct of term and overnight repurchase agreement operations through January of next year. The Desk was also instructed to engage in overnight reverse repurchase operations at an offering rate of 1.45 percent, with a per-counterparty limit of $30 billion per day. The Board also approved a 1/4 percentage point decrease in the primary credit rate to 2.25 percent, effective October 31, 2019. The Federal Reserve Board issued an Implementation Note on October 30, 2019, outlining the operational tools and approach used by the Boards of Directors of the Federal Reserve Banks of Minneapolis and San Francisco to implement monetary policy. This document reflects decisions made by the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding the details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools. The information will be updated as necessary to reflect any changes in policy. For more details on open market operations and reinvestments, visit the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website. The Federal Reserve Board also approved actions by the Boards of Directors of the Federal Reserve Banks of Boston, New York, Philadelphia, Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Chicago, St. Louis, Kansas City, and Dallas. The last update to this information was on October 31, 2019.
